findings.title: Choosing Relevance again in a search's Sort menu flips a direction it doesn't have and runs a cut search again
findings.scenario:
Results shown 3; a folder with a.log, b.log, c.log, d.log; search `*.log` (status bar `3+ items`, sort Relevance). Open Sort and View Options (or the empty-space menu's Sort By) and click the checked item Relevance.
What happens: `result_sort` becomes Relevance/descending, so the menu now shows Descending checked beside two disabled direction items. Because the answer on screen says a sort may choose its items, the search is also started again: spinner, and the rows are replaced by another run. On a broad search that run can list other items among ties, and a selected row that drops out loses its selection.
What should happen: nothing. Relevance has no direction (the manual: "Both are disabled for Relevance"). The review of sorted-search-results already made the checked Ascending/Descending items do nothing for this same reason; the checked key was missed.
findings.code_path: src/finder/toolbar.rs:775-788 lists Relevance while searching and calls `set_sort(key)` on click. src/finder/mod.rs:3169-3175 flips `ascending` whenever the chosen key is the current one; mod.rs:3182-3185 stores it and calls `result_sort_changed`. src/finder/mod.rs:2352-2357 runs the search again unless the answer on screen has `sort_chooses` false. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:1029 sets `sort_chooses` on the answer of an unsorted search whose list was cut; engine.rs:883 drops a Relevance sort, so the new run is the same plain search. src/finder/toolbar.rs:792-806 draws the two check marks. Upstream's `set_sort` only stored the order, so the flip was harmless before 26ab60c.
findings.tests_gap: tests/controls.rs:1044-1051 (in a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed) pins only `set_ascending` with the direction already had. tests/controls.rs:1099-1101 clicks Relevance only when coming from Size. No test chooses the key that is already current.
findings.fix: In `Finder::set_sort`, return early when `key == SortKey::Relevance` and the current key is Relevance (or never flip `ascending` for Relevance).
findings.test_idea: In a_sort_chooses_among_every_match_not_among_the_ones_listed, right after `set_query("*.log")` with the limit at 3: `view.update(cx, |f, cx| { f.set_sort(SortKey::Relevance, cx); assert!(!f.search_in_flight_for_test()); assert!(f.current_sort().ascending); })`. Both asserts fail today.

findings.title: With Keep Folders on Top on, a sorted cut search leaves matching folders out and lists files that belong below them
findings.scenario:
Keep Folders on Top on (`folders_first` true). Use the fixture of tests/controls.rs a_sort_by_a_word_stays_with_the_names_that_have_it: folder `ledger`, files ledger.txt (5 bytes), my-ledger-notes.txt (3000), xledgerx.txt (200). Results shown 2; search `ledger`; click the Size header.
What happens: the list is my-ledger-notes.txt, xledgerx.txt with `2+ items`. The folder `ledger`, a match with the word in its name, is not listed. Name ascending behaves the same way: the first N names are chosen, and folders whose names sort after them are missing while files are shown.
What should happen: the window orders results folders first under every sort but Relevance. The manual says Keep Folders on Top "lists folders before files whatever the sort, in every view" (line 273) and that a sorted cut search "lists the first of every match in that order" (line 314). So `ledger` should be the first of the two rows, or the manual should say that the sort chooses before folders are put on top.
The mechanism is certain from the code; whether the engine or the manual is the thing to change is a judgment call, hence medium confidence.
findings.code_path: src/finder/mod.rs:1828-1834 sorts result rows by `listing::folders_on_top` and then `listing::compare`. src/finder/mod.rs:2203-2213 builds the `SearchRequest` with `sort` and nothing about folders first. crates/fffinder-core/src/engine.rs:2166-2176 (`sort_before_cut`) orders the hits by `CutKey` and name only, and engine.rs:2077 (`cut_in_order`) cuts that list to the limit. crates/fffinder-core/src/listing.rs:158-164 is the rule the window applies afterwards to what is left. src/finder/list.rs:606-621 (`toggle_folders_first`, `folders_first_changed`) only re-sorts rows and never searches again. docs/manual.md:273 and :314 are the two promises.
findings.tests_gap: Every sort test runs with `folders_first` at its default, false (crates/fffinder-core/src/config.rs:297). The engine test hits_are_sorted_before_the_cut_as_their_entries_are_listed compares the cut with `listing::compare` alone, without `folders_on_top`.
findings.fix: Add `folders_first: bool` to `SearchRequest`, set it from `config.folders_first` in `start_search`, and have `sort_before_cut` put folders first when it is set; let `folders_first_changed` call `run_search` when the answer on screen says `sort_chooses`. Smallest alternative: one sentence in the manual's sort paragraph saying a sort chooses the items before folders are put on top.
findings.test_idea: Copy a_sort_by_a_word_stays_with_the_names_that_have_it with `folders_first` turned on before the search (through the config or the toggle_folders_first action), limit 2, query `ledger`, click `Size`, and assert `ui.names() == ["ledger", "my-ledger-notes.txt"]`. Today it is ["my-ledger-notes.txt", "xledgerx.txt"].

findings.title: In Recents, the Trash or sent results the scope bar's only chip shows as off while Search Only in is on, and clicking it restarts the same search from the top
findings.scenario:
Turn on Search Only in "Folder" in a folder, or press Back to a search that was made in its folder, which turns it on. Go to Recents (Cmd+Shift+F), type a search, select a result and scroll down.
What happens: the search is of every location (`searched_folder()` is None), but the scope bar's one chip, This Computer, is drawn unselected. Click it: the search is the same, yet it runs as a new one, so the selection is cleared and the list jumps to the top. From then on Search Only in is off for the tab.
What should happen: the chip shows as on wherever the place has no folder to search, and a click that leaves the searched place unchanged is not a new search.
The chip's test (`scope == Computer`) is upstream's. This branch adds the reset of selection and scroll (7ef1f95) and a second way into the state through Back (323f173).
findings.code_path: src/finder/bars.rs:86-96 selects the chip by `scope == SearchScope::Computer`, and bars.rs:97-109 draws the folder chip only where there is a folder. src/finder/mod.rs:2157-2162 (`searched_folder`) is what the search actually uses. src/finder/mod.rs:2360-2367 (`set_scope`) calls `run_new_search` on any change of `scope`; mod.rs:2151-2154 marks it new; mod.rs:2290-2293 clears the selection and scrolls to the top at its answer. src/finder/mod.rs:2137 (`restore_search`) is how Back sets the scope. src/finder/toolbar.rs:636 shows the toolbar's button as on only where there is a folder, so it does not disagree; only the chip does.
findings.tests_gap: a_change_of_scope_kind_or_contents_starts_at_the_top_too (tests/basics.rs) clicks the chips only in a folder, where the two scopes are different searches. No test searches from Recents, the Trash or sent results with the scope set to the folder.
findings.fix: In `render_scope_bar`, select the This Computer chip by `self.searched_folder().is_none()`. In `set_scope`, call `run_new_search` only when `searched_folder()` changed, and otherwise only store the scope.
findings.test_idea: Open a folder, call `f.set_scope(SearchScope::Folder, cx)`, navigate to Recents, search for a word with several results, select the second result, click `scope-computer`. Assert `ui.selected()` is unchanged and `!f.search_in_flight_for_test()`. Today the selection is empty after the click.

findings.title: A rename ended by a press on another item selects the renamed item again a moment later; after a right-click, the open menu acts on the renamed item, not the one it names (new in the column view, inherited in list and icons)
findings.scenario: Steps (list, icon or column view; not run, traced in the code): 1) select notes.txt, press F2, type a different valid name (say plan). 2) Without pressing Return, right-click another item, Roadmap.md. What happens: the press ends the edit and renames the file; Roadmap.md is selected and its menu opens, reading Cut "Roadmap.md", Copy "Roadmap.md", Compress "Roadmap.md". A few milliseconds later the reload that the rename asked for ends and selects plan.txt instead (the highlight jumps; Roadmap.md is deselected). The menu stays open. Every action item in it (Open, Quick Look, Get Info, Rename…, Duplicate, Cut, Copy, Copy Path, Compress, Move to Trash) reads the selection when it is chosen, so Move to Trash trashes plan.txt, the file just renamed, and Open opens it. Same with a left click followed by a key: click Roadmap.md to end the edit, press Cmd+Backspace, and plan.txt goes to the Trash. Expected: the item pressed stays selected and the menu acts on the item it names. The name must really change: an unchanged name returns before the reload (dialogs.rs:852-854). In the column view this is new with 7e8df53: before it the reload only set the rows' selection, which the column view does not read, so the column kept the right-clicked row. It now happens in the first column (select_row_in_columns) and in a further column (load_column's `wanted`). A further variant there: ending a rename in column 1 by clicking its parent folder's grey row in column 0 puts the column in use back on column 1 with the renamed file selected. The column-pane record lists only 'leaves the renamed item selected, not the clicked one' under left_out; the menu acting on another item than it names is not recorded, and nothing of it is in final-pass-notes.md.

Menu commands read the selection when chosen: src/finder/menus.rs:322-326 Move to Trash -> src/finder/trash.rs:26-45 `self.selected_entries()`; mod.rs:3013-3026 open_selected.
findings.tests_gap: tests/basics.rs:1372-1377 ('Clicking somewhere else keeps what was typed') ends a rename with a click on another row and asserts only that the new name exists and the field is gone, not what is selected. The column tests end every rename with Return (tests/basics.rs:1715-1718, 1736-1743). No test opens a menu, or presses a key, after a rename ended by a press. findings.title: Go to Folder confirmed with Return from the filter field of an open Smart Folder leaves the keyboard on a field that is no longer drawn: every key is dead until a click
findings.scenario: Steps (not run, traced in the code): 1) a Smart Folder saved with a Nushell filter is in the sidebar, and the window's own filter bar is closed. 2) Click the Smart Folder: its search runs and the filter bar opens with its filter. 3) Click in the filter field (leave the text as it is). 4) Press Cmd+Shift+G (Ctrl+L on Linux and Windows), type a folder or keep the one offered, press Return. What happens: the window goes to the folder, which ends the Smart Folder's search and puts the window's own setup back, so the filter bar goes away. The dialog then closes and the kit hands the keyboard back to what had it when the dialog opened: the filter field, which is not drawn. Keys are now dispatched from the window's root only, so the arrow keys, typing, Cmd+F, Cmd+Shift+G, Escape and the Mac menu bar's commands do nothing until something is clicked (or Tab is pressed). Expected: the files have the keyboard, as they do when the same Smart Folder is left with Cmd+[ from its filter field (tests/controls.rs:4155-4160) or with the dialog's Go button (dialogs.rs:726-729). Neither rescue reaches this case: replace_filter's own hand-off needs the field to have the keyboard at that moment, and the dialog has it; keyboard_lost acts only when the thing that lost the keyboard was inside the browser, and here it was the dialog, drawn outside it. With the dialog's exit animation the window is blurred first, so when the keyboard lands on the undrawn field no focus-lost event fires at all. The same end state follows when a second launch or `fff gui PATH` (open_request) or `fff show` (show_results) navigates the window while any dialog opened from that filter field is up. Before 60df179 a Smart Folder's filter bar stayed open after navigation, so the field was still there.
findings.code_path: src/finder/dialogs.rs:672-678 go_to_folder -> :30-35 focus_before_dialog keeps the keyboard in a focused field (`!window.has_focused_input(cx)` is false), so the kit records the filter field as the handle to return to (gpui-component-0.8.1 src/root.rs:383). Return: gpui-base-0.8.1 src/dialog.rs:586-600 Confirm -> on_ok (dialogs.rs:716-718) -> submit_go_to :747-770 -> src/finder/mod.rs:1269-1275 navigate -> :2095-2104 end_search -> src/finder/filter.rs:380-407 leave_smart_folder -> :283-302 replace_filter(before.filter, before.filter_open): filter_open = false and the filter empty, so filter_bar_open() is false; the hand-off at :298-301 needs `field.is_focused(window)`, false while the dialog's field has the keyboard. The bar is drawn only while open (mod.rs:4415-4417). The dialog then closes through request_confirm(true) -> gpui-component src/root.rs:455-485 defer_close_dialog -> `window.focus(&handle, cx)` (:482) for the filter field's handle. src/finder/mod.rs:2596-2615 keyboard_lost returns because the nearest drawn ancestor of what went is in the dialog layer, not in the browser (:2607), and gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/window.rs:3537-3545 fires focus-lost only when the frame before had a focus path. Keys then go to the root node only: gpui-pre-0.3.10 src/window.rs:6507-6515.
findings.tests_gap: tests/controls.rs:4137-4175 (the_keyboard_stays_in_the_window_when_a_smart_folder_takes_the_filter_bar_away) leaves the Smart Folder with a key that acts while the filter field itself has the keyboard (Cmd+[ and Cmd+]). The Go to Folder tests (tests/controls.rs:3331-3470) all start with the keyboard in the files. The focus-lost-recovery tests cover parts of the browser that go away and say dialogs are unchanged; no test closes a dialog whose return target has gone meanwhile.
findings.fix: A net at draw time, beside keyboard_lost: at the top of Finder's render, if `!self.filter_bar_open()` and the filter field's handle `is_focused(window)`, call focus_files and ask for one more frame with `window.defer(cx, |window, _| window.refresh())`. It covers the external navigations too. Narrower alternative, three lines: in focus_before_dialog, give the files the keyboard first when the focused field is the filter field and `smart_folder_setup.is_some()` (the bar can go with that search).
findings.test_idea: tests/controls.rs, with atlas_folders(&fx) as in the test at :4137: ui.update(|f, _, cx| f.add_smart_folder(filtered, cx)); ui.click(("smart", 0usize)); ui.click("filter-input"); ui.press(&cmd("shift-g")); ui.type_text(&fx.path("Projects").display().to_string()); ui.press("enter"); assert!(!ui.dialog_open()); assert!(!ui.exists("filter-input")); assert!(ui.files_focused()) (fails today); ui.press("down"); assert_eq!(ui.selected().len(), 1).

verdicts.evidence:
Traced by reading the snapshot at 7e8df53; no guard, reset or early return stops it.

1. src/finder/toolbar.rs:775-787 lists Relevance while searching. `.checked(sort.key == key)` only draws the mark; the item's `on_click` calls `this.set_sort(key, cx)`. The left-click reselect is in done/column-pane-selection-by-path.json under left_out, probed by that reviewer and left on purpose. If the flag is meant strictly as "any part recorded", read it as true for the left-click half only. In the list and icon views the behaviour is upstream's (66c919b); in the column view it is a regression of this branch (7e8df53).

Finding 1, two cautions on the proposed fix:
- "Apply the rename's select only if the selection is empty after rebuild_rows" breaks the gallery. rebuild_rows ends with select_first_for_gallery (mod.rs:1852, 1859-1868), which selects row 0 once the old path has dropped out, so a gallery rename would end on the first item instead of the renamed one. Decide before rebuild_rows, by path: select the new name when the selection is empty or is exactly the old path.
- A rename made in the sidebar's tree goes through the same submit_rename, so the rule also changes what the list selects after a tree rename while another item is selected.

Finding 2 is a regression of this branch: before 60df179 the bar stayed after navigation. Severity 3 because the symptom is a dead keyboard but the flow is narrow and one click recovers. The finder's narrower fix (give the files the keyboard in focus_before_dialog when the filter field of an open Smart Folder has it) also changes Cancel: the keyboard would come back to the files, not to the field. The draw-time net avoids that and covers the external navigations too.
